'''''Buxus balearica''''', the '''Balearic boxwood''', is a shrub or small evergreen tree typical of the [[Mediterranean forests, woodlands, and scrub|Mediterranean forest]]. It grows wild in [[Algeria]], Morocco, the Island of Sardinia and Spain.

==Description== 
[[File:Buxus balearica0601.jpg|thumb|240px|Young Balearic Boxwood]]

The Balearic boxwood is a [[monoecious]] tree or shrub up to three meters high. Its leaves, somewhat larger than those of the [[Buxus sempervirens|common boxwood]], are oval and bright, sometimes showing a reddish or yellowish color.<ref>{{Cite web |title=BUXUS BALEARICA |url=http://www.arbolesornamentales.es/Buxusbalearica.htm |access-date=2026-09-08 |website=www.arbolesornamentales.es}}</ref>
It blooms in spring and can be reproduced from seeds or from cuttings. Like other Mediterranean species, it is able to regenerate well after a fire.

==Distribution in Spain ==

In Spain the Balearic boxwood can be found in very fragmented populations in Eastern [[Andalusia]] and the [[Balearic Islands]].

In Eastern Andalusia, it is found in the provinces of [[Province of Málaga|Málaga]] and [[province of Granada|Granada]] in the [[Sierras of Tejeda, Almijara and Alhama Natural Park]].<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20120503014337/http://www.juntadeandalucia.es/medioambiente/contenidoExterno/Pub_revistama/revista_ma32/pinilla.html Junta de Andalucía: PARQUE NATURAL SIERRAS DE TEJEDA, ALMIJARA Y ALHAMA]</ref> 
It is also found in the [[Province of Almería]] in the [[Sierra de Gádor]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Buxus balearica |url=https://www.almerinatura.com/joyas/buxus-balearica.html |access-date=2026-09-08 |website=www.almerinatura.com}}</ref>

In the [[Balearic Islands]] it can be found in the [[Serra de Tramuntana]] of [[Mallorca]], as well as in the [[Cabrera, Balearic Islands|Island of Cabrera]], but has become extinct from the island of [[Menorca]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Herbario Virtual del Mediterráneo Occidental |url=http://herbarivirtual.uib.es:80/cas-med/especie/4147.html |archive-url=http://web.archive.org/web/20181031090316/http://herbarivirtual.uib.es:80/cas-med/especie/4147.html |archive-date=2018-10-31 |access-date=2026-09-08 |website=herbarivirtual.uib.es}}</ref>

In the [[Region of Murcia]] the species was cited in 1943 in the Sierra de la Muela, Cabo Tiñoso y Roldán, but is currently considered extinct.<ref>[http://www.floraprotegida.es/extintas.php/Buxus-balearica-1/ Flora protegida de la Región de Murcia: Buxus balearica]</ref>

In general, in Spain, it is included in the [[IUCN Red List]] of threatened vascular flora as "[[Near-threatened species|near threatened]]", in the Red List of vascular flora in Eastern Andalusia, as "[[vulnerable species|vulnerable]]".

==Distribution in Africa ==
In Morocco it can be found in the [[Rif]], in the [[Talassemtane National Park]].

;Etymology
Buxus: generic name that derives from the ancient Greek bus, Latinized buxus, buxum which is the name given to boxwood.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Flora Vascular - Toda la informaci�n detallada sobre la Flora Vascular {{!}} BioScripts.net |url=https://www.floravascular.com/index.php?genero=Buxus |access-date=2026-09-08 |website=www.floravascular.com}}</ref>
